cases.label: 27. Nxe6
cases.title: Escaping one fork target leaves the price of the other target out of the answer
cases.finding: The core records Nb3 escaping the e6-knight and surviving on a5, and closes Nxe6 Kxe6. It omits the immediate Nb3 Nxf4 exf4 exchange of the other fork target, the f4-bishop. The preceding saved comparison and current board already identify both threatened pieces.
cases.manual_english_draft: Black's e6-knight attacks both the d4-knight and f4-bishop. Nxe6 Kxe6 exchanges the two knights; Nb3 saves White's knight, but ...Nxf4 exf4 trades the bishop for Black's knight.
cases.next_task: Preserve the price of the connected threatened target as well as the escaping root mover. A narrow survival witness alone does not answer which piece is exchanged to meet the same double attack.
cases.product_basic: The recorded continuation is Nb3. Nb3 moves the knight out of the attack from Black's knight on e6. After Kg3, the white knight originally on d4 is still present on a5. In the Nxe6 Kxe6 sequence, both sides exchange one knight. With Nxe6, the white knight originally on d4 captures the black knight originally on e6; with Kxe6, the black king originally on e7 recaptures that piece.
cases.scope: Immediate exchanges in the recorded pair. No claim that one minor piece is generally better, that the capture is forced in all lines, or that the exchange explains the complete evaluation difference. Manual draft not implemented.
